_note: US-1576. The behavioural contract for the measurement-overlay editor math, asserted by BOTH src/lib/__tests__/measure-editor-math.test.ts and android/app/src/test/java/com/gradethread/app/measure/MeasureGeometryTest.kt. src/lib/measure-editor-math.ts is the spec; this file is what stops a port drifting from it. A source diff cannot be the guard - the ports are in three languages with three point types. iOS (ios/GradeThread/Measure/MeasureGeometry.swift) does NOT read this yet and differs on formatQuarter (ASCII '22 1/4' rather than the glyph); adopting it is a macOS session.
_homography: Row-major 3x3. This one is a pure 100px-per-inch scale, so every expected inch value below is checkable by hand.
_hitEndpointLines: Endpoints are ORIGINAL px; the point is DISPLAY px. Radius is given explicitly on every case because the platform DEFAULTS deliberately differ - 14 on web (cursor), 24 on iOS and Android (fingertip).
_nudge: US-2686. Moving an endpoint by keyboard (web) or by nudge button (iOS). SHARED WITH iOS ios/GradeThread/Measure/MeasureNudge.swift, which is the one place these numbers must agree: two clients that disagree about what one press moves are two clients whose logged correction deltas cannot be compared. ANDROID DOES NOT IMPLEMENT NUDGE and therefore does not read these two sections - MeasureGeometryTest.kt pulls sections BY NAME rather than iterating the file, so nothing there breaks and nothing there is stubbed. When Android grows a keyboard or switch-access path, these are already here.
_nudgeStep: Proportional to the SHORT edge, rounded, floored at 1. A fixed step is a visible jump on a 1600px phone photo and imperceptible on a 4000px camera one. The floor matters more than it looks: a step of 0 is a control that reports success and moves nothing.
_nudged: CLAMPED to the image, not refused - the same thing the drag path does. Refusing would leave someone pressing a key that silently does nothing near the border, indistinguishable from a bug. `down` increases y: these are top-left-origin image pixels, and naming the directions by what the user sees is what keeps the labels and the maths from disagreeing.
